title: At BATS, oxygen on the 26.5 density surface follows the thickness of its own mode-water density class, which thinned after 2011 and did not recover when mode water returned in 2019-2025
abstract: Question: at the Bermuda Atlantic Time-series Study (BATS), oxygen on the sigma-theta 26.5 surface fell by about 11 umol/kg from 1989-1998 to 2016-2025 and apparent oxygen utilization (AOU) increased. Is this a ventilation change or a respiration change? Approach: we used 428 BATS bottle cruises (BCO-DMO 3782 v10, 1989-2025). We calculated two ventilation indices: the total Eighteen Degree Water (EDW) thickness (17-19 degC layer) and the thickness of the density class around each surface. We fitted on 1989-2009 and tested 2010-2025 out of sample. Results: total EDW thickness explained the 2010-2018 AOU rise but failed in 2019-2025: EDW came back from 202 m to 304 m, but AOU on 26.5 stayed about 10 umol/kg above the forecast. The thickness of the 26.5 class itself predicted AOU on 26.5 well (training r = -0.73; test r = -0.95, RMSE 4.9 against 10.4 for the training mean; first-difference r = -0.74). The same holds on 26.4 and 26.6 and with cast-level profiles. The 2019-2025 mode-water recovery was in the lighter 26.4 class, where AOU recovered. The 26.5 class thinned from 152 m (2010-2011) to 67 m (2019-2025), the lowest of the record. Its thinning explains 57% (20-99%) of the 1989-1998 to 2016-2025 AOU gain with the training slope and 88% with the full-record slope. After the last strong renewal (2010-2011), AOU on 26.5 rose at 4.4 umol/kg per year (3.6-5.2), equal to the CFC/SF6 oxygen utilization rate on the nearby A22 section (4.6-4.8). Nutrient changes follow remineralization ratios. We found no change in the within-year AOU rise between 1989-1998 and 2016-2025 (-1.0 umol/kg per year, interval -6.3 to +4.3). The BATS and CalCOFI oxygen anomalies on 26.5 had different timing (r = 0.21). Conclusion: the BATS oxygen loss on 26.5 is mainly a loss of mode-water renewal in this density class; a respiration increase is not necessary, but our tests cannot exclude a small one. Limitations: the class-thickness test was defined after the total-thickness test failed; it is a correlation, not a closed budget; about 4 umol/kg in 2019-2025 stays unexplained; one site; sparse thermocline bottles; no model comparison.
